challenges.name: pointer-arithmetic-quiz
challenges.title: Where does the pointer point?
challenges.description: Predict what pointer arithmetic, indexing and the one-past-the-end pointer really do before you write an in-place function.

questions.explanation: p = a + 1 points at a[1] (20). *(p + 2) is the element two ints further: a[3] = 40. p[-1] means *(p - 1), which is a[0] = 10; a negative index is fine as long as the result stays inside the array. &a[4] - p subtracts two pointers into the same array and gives the distance in ELEMENTS, not bytes: 4 - 1 = 3, of type ptrdiff_t, printed with %td. Output: 40 10 3.

options.text: It does not compile: an index cannot be negative.

questions.explanation: a + 4 is the one-past-the-end pointer: forming it and comparing with it (end != a) is valid C, and end - a is 4 elements of type ptrdiff_t. Reading *end is undefined behaviour, because there is no element there; ASan reports it as a stack-buffer-overflow. Inside f, the parameter int a[4] is adjusted to int *a, so sizeof a is the size of a pointer (8 here), not 16; gcc even warns with -Wsizeof-array-argument. const int *q = a; makes the ints read-only through q, but q itself can still move, so q++ compiles. a + 5 is not even allowed to be computed: only pointers into the array and one past its end are valid.

options.text: end - a is 4, and its type is ptrdiff_t.
Reading *end is fine; it just gives an unspecified number.
Inside f, sizeof a is 8, not 16.
With const int *q = a; the statement q++; is a compile error.
Computing a + 5 (without reading it) is valid, like a + 4.

challenges.name: compact-scans-in-place
challenges.title: Write compact_scans(first, last, max_kept)
challenges.description: Scanner SCN-07 logs weight readings; a reading <= 0 is a misread. Write size_t compact_scans(int *first, int *last, int *max_kept) that removes the misreads from the half-open range [first, last) in place with a read pointer and a write pointer, keeps the good readings in their original order at the front, returns how many were kept, and stores the largest kept reading in *max_kept (only when at least one was kept). The test runner prints the count, the kept readings, max and whether you wrote outside the range.

tests.name: Mixed readings: misreads removed, order kept
All misreads: count 0 and max not written
INT_MIN is removed, INT_MAX is kept
Misreads at both ends, equal readings in the middle
